;Armed conflicts and attacks
*[[Nakhon Ratchasima shootings]]
**A soldier [[mass shooting|opens fire]] in a [[military camp]] and a shopping center in [[Nakhon Ratchasima]], [[Thailand]], killing 29 people and injuring 58 others before being shot dead by [[Royal Thai Police|police]] the next day. It is considered the deadliest mass shooting in the country's history. [https://www.bangkokpost.com/thailand/general/1853334/17-killed-as-soldier-opens-fire-in-korat (''Bangkok Post'')] [https://www.usatoday.com/story/news/world/2020/02/08/thailand-soldier-terminal-21-mall-shooting-rampage-korat/4700184002/ (''USA Today'')]
*At least ten people have been killed and dozens have been injured in ethnic clashes in [[Kazakhstan]] between [[Kazakhs]] and [[Dungan people|Dungans]]. About 30 houses and 15 commercial properties were destroyed during the clash. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-asia-51425938 (BBC News)]
*[[War in Afghanistan (2001–2021)]]
**A [[shootout]] during [[Military exercise#Joint exercise|joint exercises]] with [[United States Army|U.S.]] and [[Afghan National Army|Afghan soldiers]] in [[Nangarhar Province]] leaves between four and six Americans, and six Afghans dead. It is unknown if the [[Taliban]] or [[NATO Training Mission-Afghanistan#Green-on-blue attacks|rogue Afghan forces]] were responsible. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-usa-afghanistan/american-afghan-soldiers-killed-in-shootout-in-afghanistan-ny-times-idUSKBN2020Q9 (Reuters)]

;Business and economy
*[[Argentine Vice President]] [[Cristina Fernández de Kirchner]] declares that the [[government of Argentina|government]] will not pay back its [[U.S. dollar|US$]]57 billion debt to the [[International Monetary Fund]] until the country exits its [[recession]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-cuba-argentina/argentina-wont-repay-imf-debt-till-recession-over-vp-fernandez-say-idUSKBN20302R?il=0 (Reuters)]

;Health and environment
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**Two people – one [[Japanese people|Japanese]] and one [[Americans|American]] – die from coronavirus in [[Wuhan]]. They are the first foreigners (excluding [[Hong Kong]] and [[Macau]]) to die from it. [https://www.nbcnews.com/news/world/coronavirus-updates-u-s-japanese-citizens-die-wuhan-global-deaths-n1132951 (NBC News)]

;International relations
*[[Syria–Turkey relations]]
**[[Iran]]ian [[Ministry of Foreign Affairs (Iran)|Foreign Minister]] [[Mohammad Javad Zarif]] offers to mediate between [[Syria]] and [[Turkey]] over escalating conflicts between the two nations following the [[Northwestern Syria offensive (November 2019–present)|recent offensive in the Idlib Governorate]]. [https://www.reuters.com/article/us-syria-security-iran-turkey/iran-says-it-is-ready-to-mediate-between-turkey-and-syria-idUSKBN2020HO (Reuters)]

;Politics and elections
*[[2020 Irish general election]]
**Citizens of [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] head to the polls in the country's latest [[Elections in the Republic of Ireland|general election]]. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/feb/08/ireland-general-election-sinn-fein-tipped-breakthrough (''The Guardian'')]
**Exit polls show the [[Irish republicanism|republican]] [[Sinn Féin]], the ruling [[Fine Gael]], and main opposition party [[Fianna Fáil]] in a virtual tie. [https://www.theguardian.com/world/2020/feb/08/ireland-general-eleciton-sinn-fein-surge-to-22-in-exit-poll (''The Guardian'')]
